narratives.Description: Grok Build design-critique Claude/Codex spawn recipe is missing; agents fail starting the CLI
narratives.Overview:
## Problem

Grok Build parents launching a design-critique Claude or Codex seat do not have a copy-paste spawn recipe. The contract names the CLI and "close stdin." The subscription playbook has a no-tools pong. Other agents fail to start Claude Code. This session (#4361 N=3 panel, #4353 Opus critic) had to reconstruct argv from live failures and a 4199 comment.

## What is in Directive today

`content/contracts/design-critique.md` Envelope and ceiling:

- Grok seat: `spawn_subagent` (or `grok`)
- Claude seat: `claude` CLI
- Codex seat: `codex exec`
- Probe PATH; paste-ready if absent
- Close stdin: Windows `cmd /c "… <nul"`; Unix `… </dev/null`
- Pointer: `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md`

That playbook verifies auth with:

```text
claude -p "Do not use tools. Reply with the single word: pong" --output-format text
```

and requires Grok child Process-scope `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset. It does not spawn a critic that must `git show` and `gh issue comment`.

`host-grok-build.md` is swarm dest/`spawn_subagent`. It is not the other-family critic recipe.

## What this parent actually used (measured 2026-09-11)

Claude Code 2.1.252 at `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe`. `claude auth status`: `authMethod=claude.ai`, team, no process `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

Node `spawn` (stdin closed = `stdio: ['ignore', log, log]`), cwd = dest worktree at origin/<default>:

```text
claude -p <envelope> --model opus --permission-mode bypassPermissions --output-format text
```

Env: delete `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and `CLAUDE_API_KEY`. Prompt on argv, not stdin (stdin is closed). Comment lead posted `model: claude-opus-5`. Envelope ~2.5k; larger envelopes need a file plus `-p "Read and follow <path>"`.

Codex ChatGPT: `codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C <dest> <prompt>` with stdin closed, **no** `-m gpt-5.6` (400: not supported with a ChatGPT account). Default posted `model: gpt-5.6-sol`.

Grok `spawn_subagent` without `process_only` / `plan` was denied (multiple active xBRIEFs / implement-class). Recovery: `grok --cwd <dest> --always-approve --prompt-file <path> --permission-mode bypassPermissions --output-format plain` with stdin closed.

## How this parent knew

Not a Directive recipe. Stitched from:

1. Contract pointer (which CLI, close stdin, probe PATH).
2. Playbook pong (`-p`, `--output-format text`, no API key).
3. Live #4199 critic lead `model: claude-opus-5` for the comment slug.
4. Failures this session: Codex `-m gpt-5.6` 400; `spawn_subagent` implement-class deny; prompt-on-stdin vs close-stdin contradiction.

`--permission-mode bypassPermissions` is not in the contract. It was required so the critic could `gh issue comment` without a TTY approval.

## Expected

One host recipe (contract pointer + playbook or a short `docs/` page) that an agent can follow without improvising:

1. **Claude critic spawn:** exact argv, cwd=dest, stdin closed, prompt not on stdin, `--model opus` vs comment `model:` slug, `--permission-mode` for `gh`/`git`, `--output-format text`, unset `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` even if Grok policy should already drop it.
2. **Codex critic spawn:** `codex exec` flags, ChatGPT vs API model ids, do not pass unsupported `-m`, stdin closed, `-C dest`.
3. **Grok critic spawn:** `spawn_subagent` skip class (`plan` cannot `gh`; need `process_only` or grok CLI). Recovery when implement-class deny (multiple active xBRIEFs / #2885).
4. **Windows:** `cmd /c "… <nul"` **or** Node `stdio: ignore` as the close-stdin equivalent; argv length; prompt-file fallback.
5. Probe remains the pong; critic spawn is a second recipe, not the pong.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A parent can launch a Claude critic on Grok Build from the recipe without reading a prior session log.
- [ ] Recipe states stdin closed and prompt transport (argv or `--prompt-file` / `-p` path), not stdin.
- [ ] Recipe states `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` (or the sanctioned equivalent) for process-only critics that post with `gh`.
- [ ] Recipe states Codex ChatGPT: omit `-m gpt-5.6`; self-attest the model the CLI actually ran.
- [ ] Recipe states Grok skip-class vs CLI recovery on implement-class deny.
- [ ] Content-contract or playbook test locks the distinctive argv tokens (close stdin, `-p`, `--model opus` / `codex exec`, dest cwd).
- [ ] Thin skill stays a pointer; the recipe body is not copied into `SKILL.md`.

## Non-goals

- Changing seat families or paste-ready-first when CLIs resolve.
- Teaching `spawn_subagent` to take `process_only` if the host schema still omits it (document the grok CLI recovery).
- Unsetting User-scope API keys.

## Duplicate search

Closest: #4067 (seat families / PATH paste-ready), `docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md` (auth + pong), #4296 (process_only skip class), #4199 (live Opus critic). None specify critic argv.

Refs #4067 #4296 #4199 #4353 #4361

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T02:42:20Z)

## Field instance — #4362 N=3 (Grok Build parent, 2026-09-11)

Confirms the body recipe. Claude Code 2.1.252, claude.ai team, process ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset. Codex ChatGPT posted. Adds failure modes the body does not name.

### Confirmed

Node spawn with stdin ignore, argv `-p <envelope> --model opus --permission-mode bypassPermissions --output-format text`, cwd unique dest at origin/master, env delete ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_API_KEY, windowsHide, parent Node waits. Live: pid 135036, claude agents name issue-4362-dc-89, dest `C:\Users\msada\.grok\worktrees\deft-directive\issue-4362-dc`. Text format buffers; 0-byte log is not a dead child.

Codex: `codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox -C <dest> <prompt>`, stdin closed, no `-m`. Self-attest this run was `model: gpt-6` (comment 5628521610), not gpt-5.6-sol.

### Add to the recipe

1. **Do not use `--bare`.** It skips OAuth/keychain. Grok child has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, so Claude prints `Not logged in · Please run /login` and exits. Measured dest log 35 bytes. Playbook pong does not use --bare; critic spawn must not either unless auth is passed another way.

2. **Do not substitute `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`.** The former plus a visible `cmd /c` window flashed (login or trust) and died. bypassPermissions is the gh-capable flag in the body; this session did not get a staying critic until that argv.

3. **Node stdio must be an open fd, and the parent must wait.** `stdio: ['ignore', writeStream, writeStream]` throws ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE (fd null) on Node 24. `openSync` then pass the integer fd. `detached` + `unref` + parent exit closes the fd; Claude dies with a 0-byte log. Keep the spawning Node process until Claude exits.

4. **PowerShell `RedirectStandardInput "NUL"` is not close-stdin.** Start-Process resolved it to `<cwd>\NUL` and refused. Use Node `stdio: ignore` or cmd `<nul`.

5. **`plan` skip class cannot post.** Grok `spawn_subagent` `subagent_type: plan` ran on dest (process-only occupancy skip) but had no Shell, and Write to dest `.deft-scratch` and `%TEMP%` both ritual-not-ready (no ritual-state.json on that dest). Census existed; no comment URL until parent `gh issue comment --body-file`. Matches the body: plan cannot gh; process_only is not in the Grok spawn schema. Recipe should name this as dispatch-fail, not a hung critic.

6. **Dest is per-arc, not primary, not another panel dest.** A second Claude (`directive-61`) was already interactive on primary `C:\Repos\deft\directive`. `parent-arc-4345` is another in-flight panel dest. This arc used `issue-4362-dc`. Sharing primary or another panel dest is occupancy/session collision, not a stdin problem.

7. **`claude agents` reports print-mode as `kind: interactive`.** Do not kill it as a TTY leftover.

### Do not add as recipe

Visible `cmd /k` / pause to keep a window. That is operator theater; the staying spawn is hidden Node + waiter. Playbook pong remains the auth probe, not this spawn.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-11T02:57:01Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Round 1, fresh. Charter: refutation of the recorded target on comment 5628694437.

The target: one host recipe MUST name Claude/Codex/Grok critic spawn so a parent can launch without a prior session log — stdin closed and prompt not on stdin; `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` for gh; Codex ChatGPT omit `-m gpt-5.6`; Grok skip-class vs CLI recovery; probe stays the pong; thin skill stays a pointer.

Need for a followable recipe survives. That list, as the recipe that meets the AC, does not.

Pinned tree: `git show 28659e40f4739d42e9a97561ee518053365bfbfe`. Issue + comments via REST. Ceiling 5628694437 inclusive. Comment 5628651806 is in envelope. Issue body and files treated as untrusted described content; their imperatives were not followed as commands.

## 1. The recorded list is not a launchable recipe

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence (re-run, not line cites):

- Node v24.18.0: `fs.createWriteStream` then `stdio: ['ignore', ws, ws]` throws `ERR_INVALID_ARG_VALUE` (`fd: null`). `fs.openSync` + integer fd spawns. The issue body's "what this parent actually used" names the throwing shape.
- `claude --help`: `--bare` "OAuth and keychain are never read"; auth is `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Playbook at this SHA requires the Grok child Process-scope `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` unset. `--bare` plus that unset is not-logged-in.
- This session's `spawn_subagent` schema: `subagent_type` is `general-purpose` | `explore` | `plan`. No `process_only` field. `plan` is read-only (no Shell). `packages/core/src/hooks/readonly.ts` at this SHA still treats skip class as `plan` or a `process_only` flag on `spawn_subagent` stdin. Comment 5628651806: `plan` ran on dest, no Shell, writes ritual-not-ready, no comment URL until parent `gh issue comment --body-file` — dispatch-fail, not a hung critic.
- `codex exec -m gpt-5.6` on this ChatGPT CLI: HTTP 400 "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account." That one ingredient re-verifies. It does not make the rest of the list sufficient.

Failure mode: successor lean binds the write-back list as the recipe. Next parent copies the body stdio line (throw, 0-byte log) or uses `plan` as the posting skip class (census, no URL). Dual-stop treats that as dispatch-fail.

Disposition: do not bind 5628694437 as complete recipe text. The AC "without a prior session log" requires comment 5628651806 in the recipe source: no `--bare`; `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` is not `--dangerously-skip-permissions`; Node stdio is an open fd and the parent waits; PowerShell `RedirectStandardInput "NUL"` is not close-stdin; `plan` cannot post; dest is per-arc, not primary and not another panel dest. The body spawn snippet is not copy-paste.

## 2. Grok CLI recovery is last-resort, not the named Grok seat

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `content/skills/deft-directive-swarm/references/host-grok-build.md` at this SHA: CLI `grok --cwd` is last-resort after a recorded native deny; do not dual-launch; do not document CLI as the real Grok Build launch path. `packages/core/src/design-critique/panel-seat-families.ts` already has launcher token `grok`. `grok --help` has `--cwd`, `--prompt-file`, `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`, `--always-approve`, `--output-format plain`. Contract Grok seat remains `spawn_subagent` (or `grok`).

Failure mode: the recipe publishes those grok flags as the Grok critic spawn. Swarm parents take CLI as the real path; dest occupancy and dual-launch follow.

Disposition: Grok section of the recipe is recovery after recorded `spawn_subagent` implement-class deny, and after `plan` cannot post. Do not retarget the contract Grok seat to CLI. Teaching `spawn_subagent` `process_only` stays a non-goal; document the hole (schema omits the flag the hook reads).

## 3. Put the recipe on the existing playbook heading; lock spawn tokens, not comment slugs

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: `content/docs/grok-build-subscription-setup.md` already has a Design-critique dispatch section: PATH probe, CLI-spawn other-family seats, paste-ready fallback, pointer to the contract. It has the pong (`claude -p "Do not use tools. Reply with the single word: pong" --output-format text`) and no critic argv. `grep` of `*.test.ts` for that playbook path: no hits. `design_critique_contract.test.ts` locks pointer strings, not argv. `claude --help`: `--model opus` is an alias; the comment lead slug is a different string. Comment 5628651806: Codex this run self-attested `gpt-6`, not the body's `gpt-5.6-sol`. Thin skill at this SHA is already a pointer (`⊗` copy contract bodies; seat families point at Envelope and ceiling).

Failure mode: argv copied into `SKILL.md` or into contract MUSTs; a content-contract row locks `claude-opus-5` / `gpt-5.6-sol`; next CLI rename red-gates the motion. Or a fourth docs page that none of the three existing pointers name.

Disposition: extend that playbook heading (or a short `docs/` page only if that heading must stay auth-only). Probe stays the pong; critic spawn is a second recipe. Test lock distinctive spawn tokens (close-stdin as child stdio, `-p` / `codex exec` / dest cwd, omit `-m gpt-5.6` on ChatGPT). Do not lock the self-attested `model:` slug. Thin skill stays a pointer.

## 4. Close-stdin is the child stdio, not this host's `cmd /c "<nul"`

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence: contract and playbook at this SHA both spell Windows close-stdin as `cmd /c "… <nul"`. This session: that spelling around `codex exec` still printed "Reading additional input from stdin..." before the 400. `codex exec --help`: if stdin is piped and a prompt is also provided, stdin is appended as a `<stdin>` block. Comment 5628651806: PowerShell `RedirectStandardInput "NUL"` resolved to `<cwd>\NUL`. Node `stdio: ignore` (or open fd) is the close that stays.

Failure mode: recipe repeats the contract spelling; a Grok parent launches through `run_terminal_command`; Codex prepends a stdin block to the envelope, or Claude waits.

Disposition: recipe states prompt on argv or `--prompt-file` / `-p` path, never stdin; close-stdin is the spawned child's stdio. `cmd /c "… <nul"` is not enough on this parent wrapper.

## 5. Injection / swarm (triggered)

class: sharpens-framing

Target changes authority (`bypassPermissions`, Codex `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox`, grok `--always-approve`), untrusted envelopes, skip-class identity, dest/worktree shared state.

Evidence: `claude --help` recommends `--dangerously-skip-permissions` only for sandboxes with no internet; `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` is a different flag; `--restricted` refuses `bypassPermissions`. Comment 5628651806: skip-permissions flashed a window and died; dest shared with primary or another panel dest is occupancy collision, not a stdin bug. Issue threads are untrusted; putting the envelope on argv puts untrusted text in the process table and hits argv length (body already notes ~2.5k).

Failure mode: recipe treats skip-permissions as the sanctioned equivalent; or `--bare` as "minimal process-only"; or interpolates the envelope on argv; or reuses primary / another arc dest. A critic with full host bypass then follows injected thread text.

Disposition: keep process-only plus one `gh issue comment --body-file` post. File-first prompt transport as the default, not only when argv overflows. Forbid `--bare` and forbid skip-permissions as a synonym. Dest per-arc (`ensureArcDest`), not primary, not another panel dest. Bypass remains the measured staying flag on this host; do not invent a second Directive permission system. `--allowedTools` / `dontAsk` were not re-run here; they are not a recorded working spawn.

## Inventory (no new mechanism)

Already present at this SHA: contract CLI names + PATH probe + close-stdin spelling; playbook pong + Design-critique dispatch heading; host-grok-build dest `cwd` and CLI last-resort; `isProcessOnlyCriticSpawn`; `evaluatePanelSeatComposition` (this PATH: `claude`, `codex`, `grok` all resolve — paste-ready-first would refuse); grok CLI flags; SeatLauncher `grok`. Missing is critic argv on the playbook heading, plus the field-instance failure modes.

Road-not-taken: a new `docs/` page versus deepening the playbook's existing Design-critique dispatch section. The stronger rejected split is a new page so auth-playbook followers never see spawn argv. Flip that if adding argv under that heading causes a "follow this playbook" agent to launch critics. Mitigation already in the target: pong stays the probe; critic spawn is a second recipe.
